solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jade company retaining line over year

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits over, above, the next
the company abbreviation holds the line letter within it

explanation.surface: A firm keeps a jade necklace on its books, with a production line running for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jade' is not the green stone but the verb meaning to tire or sate.
explanation.definitionFit: To jade is to weary through excess, the same as making something sickeningly surfeiting.

clue.text: Take on horse after endless difficulty

indicators.note: the horse comes after the trimmed word
without its end, the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a stew is a state of worry or difficulty, as in 'in a stew'
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: A rider tackles a horse after a long struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb synonyms: to step into a role is to take it on or assume it.

clue.text: Discourage females

definitions.meaning: to discourage enthusiasm is to damp it down
read as two words, a dam is a mother animal and a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A curt instruction to put women off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer in two: DAM, a mother of livestock, and PEN, a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen enthusiasm is to discourage it, as wetting a fire stops it burning.

clue.text: See payment for accommodation accepted by upstanding Italian city-dweller

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the other pieces, as if accepting them

parts.note: a fine, upstanding citizen: upstanding means fine, excellent
LO is an old word for see or behold
rent is what a tenant pays for housing

explanation.surface: Seeing rent accepted by an honest Italian landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but it is simply FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Florentine is a native or resident of Florence, an Italian city.

clue.text: Writer was aware of recommendation

parts.note: to have felt something is to have sensed or been aware of it
a tip is a piece of advice or recommendation

explanation.surface: An author knew about a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A felt-tip is a pen, an instrument people write with.

clue.text: I will avoid poor showings by end of game? Not so

indicators.note: the last letter sits beside the trimmed word
the letter I keeps out of the word, so it is removed

parts.note: fails are failures, poor showings

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A player vows to avoid flops before the match ends, which proves untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will avoid' is a deletion: the letter I is what goes, not a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is not so is untrue, a synonym for incorrect.

clue.text: Construction of minute car type requires several examples of this!

definitions.text: Construction of minute car type requires several examples of this!

indicators.note: the letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Building a tiny model of a car needs several of the inflatable rubber items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Construction of' rearranges MINUTECARTYPE; the whole clue also describes the answer, as any car needs four of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable rubber wheel cover is something a car of any size fits in sets of four.

clue.text: Share vote (Labour's third, out of it)

indicators.note: the selected letter is removed from the voting word

parts.note: a ballot is a vote

indicators.note: the third letter of the next word is chosen

explanation.surface: A political aside about a share of the vote, Labour coming third and out of the running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour's third' is B, which 'out of it' removes from BALLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to apportion or distribute, a verb synonym of share out.

clue.text: Front of torpedo was wet and pointed

indicators.note: the first letter of the weapon word is taken

parts.note: when it rained the weather was wet

explanation.surface: A submarine scene: the torpedo nose got wet and was aimed.
explanation.definitionFit: To train a gun on someone is to aim it, so trained means aimed or directed.

clue.text: Young fellow about to bet and behave badly

indicators.note: the young man word goes around the betting word

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky or conceited young man
to lay a bet is to wager

explanation.surface: A lad is about to gamble and get into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who play up misbehave, a phrasal verb meaning act naughtily.

clue.text: Call back about fire in the sky

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the fire word
the naming word is read backwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
a pyre is a heap for burning, a fire

explanation.surface: A shout returns about a blaze in the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses only the Call word, giving EMAN, before 'about' splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: The empyrean is the highest heaven, so it is a poetic word for the heavens above.

clue.text: Star portraying FBI agent after introductory episode?

indicators.note: the agent comes after the introduction

parts.note: a lead-in is an introductory part
a G-man is a US federal agent, especially of the FBI

explanation.surface: An actor playing an FBI agent, following a pilot episode.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal male actor in a production is its star, its top-billed performer.

clue.text: Evil conflation of love and malice

indicators.note: a blending together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A moral observation that evil is love and malice fused.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoniacal describes behaviour like a demon's, devilish and wicked.

clue.text: Square number unspecified? The writer's dismissing 1,000

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

indicators.note: the thousand letter is sent away from the possessive word

parts.note: the setter's own, so mine
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A writer won't give a number and drops a thousand from their figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unspecified' gives N; 'dismissing' removes M from MINE, leaving INE.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times three is nine, making it a perfect square integer.

clue.text: Break over: judge to imprison male, as long as one remembers?

parts.note: a time-out is a break in play
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the judging word holds the male letter inside it

parts.note: to find is to judge, as a jury finds a defendant guilty

explanation.surface: Recess has ended and a judge is about to jail a man.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a very long period: since beyond the reach of anyone's memory.

clue.text: Working dog consuming a volume

indicators.note: the tracking word swallows the other letters

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or trail them

explanation.surface: A working dog eats a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like an adjective for the dog but is the definition, a noun sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail means painful labour or toil, the act of working hard.

clue.text: Fellow doesn't keep up with trendy leading example

parts.note: one who lags falls behind
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: A man falls behind a fashionable role model.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagship is the best or most important of a group, its leading model.

clue.text: Ocean current will have staff coming round

indicators.note: the staffing word encircles the current letter

parts.note: to man a place is to staff it
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A sea current will have crew coming round.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Clownish figure: President when seizing new source of drink

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US President

indicators.note: the word for when grips the new letter

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A clown and a president as a new drink brand is seized.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a famous British circus clown.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa beans are the seeds from which chocolate drinks are made.

clue.text: Conservative Party upset expert

indicators.note: in a down clue the party word is turned upside down

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: A Tory party is disrupted by a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REVEL into LEVER beneath C.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and expert are adjectives for someone skilful and able.

clue.text: No Hearts limiting openings for regular team card player

indicators.note: the outer letters bound the openings, like limits

parts.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A bridge player has no hearts for the usual team.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, the seat names name the players, so one of them is a card player.

clue.text: Vandalised grave standing in for one show of uncivilised behaviour

indicators.note: the mixed letters stand inside the example word

parts.note: say means for example, for one

indicators.note: damaged, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A vandalised grave is held up as an example of brutal conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vandalised' makes AVAGER; 'for one' is the example word, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Savagery is wild, brutal conduct, the opposite of civilised manners.

clue.text: Screw, sadly, set back railway

indicators.note: the sorrowful word is put backwards

parts.note: alas is said sadly

explanation.surface: A screw sadly reset, holding back a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is old slang for wages; 'set back' turns ALAS into SALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British slang for wages or pay, as in 'on a good screw'.

clue.text: Elevated energy in quantity of water leads to discharge

indicators.note: the energy letter is raised to a higher place in the down entry

parts.note: a lake is a body of water
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Raising energy in water levels leads to an outflow.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'Elevated' moves E up from the end of LAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak is an escape of liquid or gas, an unintended discharge.

clue.text: Abandon yeast? Not entirely

indicators.note: the raising word is not complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: leaven is a raising agent such as yeast

explanation.surface: A baker asks whether to give up on yeast, partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter, N, from LEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone is to desert or forsake them.

clue.text: Bread identified in brief epistle's words at the end

indicators.note: the bread is found inside the shortened letter name

parts.note: Eph is the short form of Ephesians, a New Testament epistle
pitta or pita is a flat bread

explanation.surface: Bread turns up in the closing lines of a short letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is an inscription on a tombstone, writing after someone's death.
